key_insight: 4D-HOF turns coarse foundation-model hand-object estimates into stable 4D interaction reconstructions by learning a conditional flow that refines pose, rotation, and alignment during generation.
engineering_relevance: The approach reduces reliance on expensive per-sequence optimization and offers a feed-forward path to robust hand-object reconstruction for real-world robotics and vision systems.
method: Uses conditional flow matching to transport initial hand-object states toward an interaction manifold.
Injects test-time guidance from physical interaction constraints and observed 2D evidence directly into the generative trajectory.
Trains on diverse datasets to improve generalization to in-the-wild scenes.
evidence_signal: The paper reports state-of-the-art results on out-of-domain benchmarks, indicating stronger stability and accuracy than prior methods.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality of foundation-model initial estimates and on reliable constraint/2D evidence at test time.
paper_title: 4D-HOF: Hand-Object Flow Matching for Feed-Forward 4D Interaction Reconstruction
